                    ### Question
                    An 8-month-old boy is brought to the emergency room by his mother who notes that the child has not been passing stool regularly. Palpation and radiographic imaging of the umbilical region reveal the presence of fecal material in an abnormal out-pocketing of bowel. Which of the following is a common complication seen in this condition?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Enlarged rugal folds
opb. Dysplasia
opc. Ulceration
opd. Megacolon
ope. Paneth cell metaplasia

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
In an 8-month-old with an abnormal out-pocketing of bowel like Meckel's diverticulum, a common complication is inflammation leading to possible ulceration. Another complication is obstruction, which can lead to megacolon. Evidence supports ulceration and megacolon as complications in this scenario.
